mitigation_mechanism: Planted mangroves are credited with sheltering the coast and what lies behind it from typhoons. In northern Viet Nam a storm in 1987 caused serious damage to a three km-stretch of sea-dyke that cost 300,000 US dollars to repair, while during the 2005 storm the same dyke did not sustain any damage, which the evaluation attributes to the protective capacity of the mangrove forests [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1]; damage to private property fell further, from 90 per cent of shrimp farm value destroyed in 1996 to 25 per cent ten years later [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_2]. Behind planted Sonneratia mangroves in Hainan, China, mean and extreme wind speed during typhoons were reduced by 59.4% and 53.2% [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mcivor12_1]. An independent World Bank evaluation in Vietnam's southern Mekong Delta draws the lesson that where reforestation was successful, land is accreting and farming and other economic activities are protected from storms, wind, and salt [ev_frmg_vnppar_8]. A project-experience paper from coastal Bangladesh states that mangrove afforestation is a soft adaptation measure that has significantly contributed to reduce the loss of life and property against tropical cyclones in coastal areas [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ahammad13_1].

A project-experience paper from coastal Bangladesh states that mangrove afforestation has significantly contributed to reduce the loss of life and property against tropical cyclones [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ahammad13_1]. An independent World Bank evaluation in Vietnam's southern Mekong Delta draws the lesson that where reforestation was successful, land is accreting and farming and other economic activities are protected from storms, wind, and salt [ev_frmg_vnppar_8].
justification.conditionality: The Viet Nam results are uncontrolled before-and-after comparisons attributed to mangroves by evaluators of the implementing Red Cross programme, and the global model concerns existing rather than restored mangroves [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_menendez20_1]. Protection weakens where the surge is largest: in Orissa the death-reducing effect was smaller for above-mean storm surges [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_dasvincent09_3], and no mangrove effect on fully collapsed houses was visible within 10 km of the coast, where many houses were swept away instead [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_das11_2]. A review finds that observational studies have not given conclusive results on how much protection mangroves provide [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_marois15_2]. The Orissa, Central American and global community studies are quasi-experimental comparisons of places with more or less existing mangrove, so they measure the service of keeping mangroves rather than the performance of planted stands, and the Florida surge figure is a model result cited in a review [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_marois15_3]. The Bhitarkanika survey also holds the results that run the other way: damage to livestock in money terms was higher in the mangrove village than in the unprotected one (127.63 against 54.05 INR per household); costs for reconstruction per household did not differ between villages, and the smaller loss of fish seedlings in the mangrove village was not significant [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_badola05_4, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_badola05_8, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_badola05_9]. Together with the Orissa finding of no effect on fully collapsed houses near the coast, these no-benefit and reversal results discount the class only slightly. The Bhitarkanika paddy comparison gives no normal-year yield per village, and villagers near the forest credit mangroves with higher productivity in general, so part of the yield gap may be a baseline difference rather than storm protection [ev_crop_yield_badola05_6]; the authors call the evidence only indicative. Like the other Orissa studies, Bhitarkanika measures existing forest with no planting involved; these units count in this family's pool because it gathers mangrove coastal-protection evidence, and they show what keeping a mangrove belt protects rather than what planting achieves. The Bangladesh statement is written by staff of the implementing project, cites a co-author's earlier work, and describes no monitoring or counterfactual [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ahammad13_1]. The Mekong Delta lesson is the evaluator's synthesis of field findings, not a measurement, and the same passage records the reverse where mangrove seedlings were planted too small, at too shallow a depth and not carefully monitored: there the coastline is moving inland, endangering the dikes built to protect the resettled areas [ev_frmg_vnppar_8]. The contrast separates what standing mangroves do from what planting achieves: the Orissa, Central American and global comparisons measure existing forest, while the Vietnam evaluation found farming protected where the planting succeeded and the coastline moving inland where the seedlings failed.

mitigation_mechanism: Mangrove tree damage rises rapidly once tropical-cyclone winds exceed 130 km/h, and extreme events with very high water levels and wind speeds may severely damage or destroy mangrove areas, leaving them less able to reduce surge [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_gijsman21_1, ev_establishment_survival_mcivor12_1]. In Florida the 2005 Hurricane Wilma was estimated to have initially destroyed 1250 ha of mangroves, and frequent hurricanes have changed some mangrove stands to mudflats [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_marois15_1]. In Vietnam's Bac Lieu province mangrove replanting was less successful, mostly because of heavy storms and flooding and poor planting techniques, and project staff told the evaluation mission that a severe storm arriving before the roots could take a firm hold in the sand would take out enough seedlings to require yet another replanting [ev_frmg_vnppar_6, ev_frmg_vnppar_7]. On the Bangladesh coast, project staff report that cyclonic shocks caused severe damages of both the Sundarbans and planted mangroves through species loss and creating large gaps [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ahammad13_4].
caveats: Compilers judge mangrove regeneration in Senegal as coping well with local windstorms and mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh as coping moderately with tropical storms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1442_2011_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_4300_2019_tropical_storm]. The review units, including the Florida loss estimate, are cited findings for existing mangrove forests, not measurements on restored stands [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_gijsman21_1, ev_establishment_survival_mcivor12_1, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_marois15_1]. Only the Vietnam and Bangladesh accounts concern planted stands, and none is a measurement: the Vietnam units are evaluator and project-staff reports, and the Bac Lieu losses mix storms, flooding and poor planting technique [ev_frmg_vnppar_6, ev_frmg_vnppar_7]; the Bangladesh statement comes from staff of the implementing project, gives no extent of the loss, and its 'severe' describes the damage, not the storm [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ahammad13_4]. The exposure is sharpest before the roots take hold, so the threat to an investment sits in the establishment years.
